script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: Paul’s apostleship is a fact from outside the passage, but no reference is given for it.
The joke about the flour’s family name does not make a clear comparison with relying on family background.
“I’m keeping his words just as he gave them” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The passage says Israel pursued righteousness, but it does not say they never gave up or kept chasing it.
Calling the Israelites Paul’s people uses a fact not established in this passage without a supporting reference.
The explanation repeats the answer without adding much and sounds flat.
The oven and timer comparison does not clearly match zeal that is not based on knowledge. The heat and counting add to the confusion.
Papa mentions a grandmother, inventing a family member when his family consists only of his six cookie cutter kids.
Calling singing a fun guess does not make the explanation funny; the rest is a flat restatement.
The oven-mitt joke makes the object being fetched stand in for Christ, putting Him at the center of the joke.
“It’s still fresh in your head” assumes what the individual baker remembers or is thinking.
Near is not the opposite of hidden, and the hidden-cookie comparison does not clearly illustrate the word being near.
The joke compares Papa’s giving with the Lord’s giving, casting Papa in God’s role for the comparison.
“Nobody needs a building here” goes beyond what Paul says. He asks how people can hear without someone to preach; he does not make a claim about buildings.
“Some did and some didn’t” asserts that some welcomed the good news. The verse says only that not all welcomed it.
The explanation says some welcomed the good news, but the verse says only that not all welcomed it.
“Someone hears, and faith comes” suggests hearing automatically produces faith. Paul has just said that not all welcomed the good news.
The lost-keys joke turns the One speaking in the quotation into the object of the comparison, making the holy subject part of the joke.
The explanation mostly tells the baker to reread the words instead of explaining them, and it sounds flat.
